Well, I've been farming these 60 mu for 40 years now, since I was a little boy following my father around the fields. I'm 48 this year. I only finished primary school, but I know my land and I know what works. My family has four people, and my wife and my older child both work part-time at the factory in town, so they're not always around when I need help. That means I have to hire labor during busy times, but I watch every yuan because cash in hand matters when someone gets sick or the pump breaks.

Last year my wheat did okay — about 420 kg per mu — and the maize was decent too. My neighbor Lao Wang tried a new wheat variety and got a bit more, so I'll use the same improved seed this year. I mostly do what I did last year. Change is risky, and I can't afford a bad year.

**My 20 mu of wheat and maize:** The wheat goes in early October. After the maize comes out, I plow the field and harrow it before planting. I put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and then at jointing time in spring, if the wheat looks yellow, I spread another 20 to 25 jin of urea. I irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once at heading. The well water costs money to pump, so I don't water more than that unless it's very dry — electricity bills add up fast. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see aphids I spray insecticide. The maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. That week is always crazy — I hire a machine to plant it fast because the window is tight. I buy hybrid seed; it's more expensive but the yield is better. I put compound fertilizer in the holes at planting, about 40 jin per mu, and topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high. Maybe water once or twice in summer if the rain doesn't come.

**My 24 mu of spring peanut:** This is important for cash. I plant in late April when the soil is warm enough. I save some seed from last year but mix in fresh seed because saved seed doesn't sprout as well — this saves some money. Peanut doesn't need as much nitrogen as grain, but I still put down about 40 to 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base. The key times for water are flowering and pod filling, so I irrigate twice. I have to watch for leaf spot disease — I spray fungicide two or three times, and herbicide at the start. Harvesting peanut is hard work, lots of digging and picking. I hire several people to help; my family alone can't finish it.

**My 16 mu of cotton:** Cotton makes good money when the price is right, but it's a lot of work and the insects are a constant headache. I plant in mid-April. I put down fertilizer before planting and topdress again at flowering. I irrigate twice — once at flowering and once at boll stage. For pests, especially bollworm, I spray when I actually see damage, not just on a schedule. Last year I sprayed too much preventively and spent too much money without getting much more cotton. Picking takes forever — I hire people for that because my family doesn't have enough hands.

All together, I'll spend about 41,000 yuan on inputs this year. That's a lot of money. I thought about buying more fertilizer for everything, but my daughter might need school fees and we need some cash in the house for emergencies. Better to be a bit conservative than to run out of money. If the weather is decent, I should get about 420 kg/mu from wheat, 480 kg/mu from maize, 300 kg/mu from peanut, and maybe 280 kg/mu of seed cotton.
